items.title: A closed subscheme is an effective Cartier divisor if and only if it is locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is the standard local characterization of effective Cartier divisors: for a closed subscheme D of a scheme S, being locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor is equivalent to the ideal sheaf I_D being invertible (statement lines 2402-2413). The proof is short but runs both directions of the equivalence and needs the dictionary between an invertible ideal sheaf, a free generator f of its sections over an affine open, and the closed subscheme Spec(A/(f)); the passage from I_D restricted to U being O_U to the injectivity of multiplication by f, and the use of quasi-coherence of I_D to identify D cap U, are the non-formal moves (proof lines 2416-2421 and 2426-2432). It is H2: no hypothesis on S beyond being a scheme is used and the argument is a local computation, but no step is replaced by a citation.
